strings.name: John Williams
strings.summary: Born into a musical family in New York, John Williams studied piano and composition, progressing from studio pianist to film composer. His scores for Jaws, Star Wars, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Schindler’s List use distinctive orchestral themes in screen storytelling. He also composed concertos and Olympic music and conducted the Boston Pops for many years, connecting film music with concert-hall performance.
strings.coverageNote: Selected early studies, major scores, conducting and a September 2026 public performance, checked through November 13, 2026; not a complete catalogue or health record.
strings.influence.rationale: Composing scores for films including Star Wars and Jaws, he used orchestral themes to shape the cinematic sound memories familiar to generations of audiences.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Flushing, Queens, New York, United States
strings.facts.f2.label: Musical training
strings.facts.f2.value: UCLA, private composition lessons and piano study at Juilliard
strings.highlights.h1.title: Orchestral themes for the screen
strings.highlights.h1.text: Linked distinctive themes with film characters and situations in scores including Jaws and Star Wars.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From screen to concert hall
strings.highlights.h2.text: Composed concertos and led the Boston Pops from 1980 to 1993.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Made a surprise conducting appearance
strings.timeline.t1.text: Conducted The Imperial March as an encore at a tribute concert at the Hollywood Bowl, returning to public performance at ninety-four.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Received the AFI Life Achievement Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became the first composer to receive the award, honoring his career in film music.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Scored Schindler’s List
strings.timeline.t3.text: Composed the score for Spielberg’s film, with Itzhak Perlman as violin soloist; won the Oscar the following year.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Composed Olympic music
strings.timeline.t4.text: Olympic Fanfare and Theme premiered with the Boston Pops and became associated with the Los Angeles Olympics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Boston Pops conductor
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Arthur Fiedler, expanding the orchestra’s repertoire, recordings and television performances; served until 1993.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Scored Star Wars
strings.timeline.t6.text: Created a distinctive musical world for George Lucas’s space film through symphonic writing and character themes.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Scored Jaws
strings.timeline.t7.text: Worked with Spielberg, using a concise, urgent musical motif to intensify suspense and threat.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Won his first Oscar
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won for his musical adaptation for the 1971 film Fiddler on the Roof, before further developing original film scores.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Studied at Juilliard
strings.timeline.t9.text: After arranging and conducting for service bands, moved to New York to study piano with Rosina Lhevinne.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Born into a New York musical family
strings.timeline.t10.text: Born in Flushing, New York; his percussionist father introduced him early to studios and orchestral sound.
